title: Product recognition and identification
purpose: Identify the requested product at the shelf reliably, primarily via barcode and OCR against a product catalog, with visual re-identification as a later enhancement.
architecturalScope: ProductDiscovery bounded context. ProductCatalogPort and a ProductMatcher service. Depends on Perception outputs; independent of any retailer API.
domainContext: Product, ProductCandidate, ProductIdentifier, BoundingBox, Confidence. Emits ProductCandidateDetected and TargetProductConfirmed.

milestones.title: Catalog + barcode identification
milestones.description: GTIN resolves to a product name offline from a cached catalog.

milestones.title: OCR-based fallback matching
milestones.description: Fuzzy matching of OCR text against catalog names.

milestones.title: Visual re-identification (experimental)
milestones.description: Embedding match against reference images as an optional aid.

tasks.title: Select catalog source and license model
tasks.description: Open Food Facts (ODbL) vs local list; document share-alike duties.
acceptanceCriteria: Data source and license obligations documented.

tasks.title: Define ProductCatalogPort and ProductResolver
acceptanceCriteria: Domain tests cover found, ambiguous and not-found cases.

tasks.title: Implement OCR fuzzy matcher
tasks.description: Rank candidates with explicit scores; never fabricate a match.
acceptanceCriteria: Low confidence yields a question, not a guess.

tasks.title: Feasibility study: visual re-identification
tasks.description: Assess whether embeddings help without barcode/OCR.

acceptanceCriteria: Barcode path: GTIN resolves correctly for the test catalog.
No product is reported as confirmed without corroborating evidence.
Product not found is communicated honestly.

risks.description: Free visual SKU recognition is not achievable on a phone.
risks.mitigation: Treat barcode/OCR as the primary path; visual ID is optional research.

risks.description: Catalog license (ODbL) imposes share-alike on derived databases.
risks.mitigation: Document and, if needed, isolate derived data.

safetyImplications: Confirming the wrong product must trigger an explicit uncertainty message.
accessibilityImplications: Identification results must be spoken clearly, including confidence qualifiers.
privacyImplications: No images of products are retained beyond ephemeral processing.
No personal purchase history is stored.
verificationRequirements: Catalog and matcher unit tests with adversarial OCR text.
Measured identification accuracy on a labelled test set.

decisionLog.decision: MVP identification uses a general VLM via todo.vision-product-search; barcode/OCR/catalog is the post-MVP reliability path researched here.
